title.narrative: Business Partnerships and Solutions for SDGs
Samarbete med privata näringslivet för hållbart företagande

description.narrative:
Projektet avser att öka förståelse för och engagera det albanska privata näringslivet för ett hållbarare företagande och bidra till de hållbarhetsmålen. Projektet kommer att skapa förutsättningar för det privata näringslivet att spela en aktiv roll i arbetet med hållbarhetsmålen genom att öppna upp möjligheter för den albanska privata sektorn att samarbeta med svenska näringslivet som ligger i framkant vad gäller utveckling mot hållbarhet (speciellt inom textil) för att gynna tillväxt samtidigt som det kommer samhällen tillgodo. De förväntade outputs är: 1.Inventering och analys av synsätt på SDG bland privata näringslivet och utveckling av ”roadmap” för Albanien inom agro-processing och textil sektorn 2.Öka förståelse för SDG: er och fördelarna med att anta SDG principer för privata näringslivet. 3.Bedöma behov av/Designa Challenge fund
Projektet löper under ett år och genomförs i huvudsak av FN-aktörer (UNDP, FAO, UNIDO och ILO). Erfarenheter från SLSD och andra i regionen kommer att utgöra en viktig del. Under denna designas kommer fokuset ligga på att samla in fakta, kartlägga och utforska nya sätt att stötta albanska privata sektorn att engagera sig och bidra till hållbarhetsmålen.

The aim of the intervention is to raise awareness and engage the private sector actors to adopt the principles of SDGs. The project will work on establishing business partnerships that will bring together businesses from Sweden, Albania as well as government and civil society representatives to test new models of engagement that will create win-win, sustainable and scalable solutions for all stakeholders in achieving the SDGs. The expected outputs of the projects are. 1. Develop a roadmap to adopting the EU Green Agenda/SDG in target sectors, agro-rpoessing and textile industry. 2. Sensitized private sectors on Economic, Social and governance benefit of adopting SDGs principles in two sectors 3. Assess and design economic schemes that will support companies in implementing sustainable projects and organisational changes connected to the SDGs. The project is a one-year intervention implemented by UN agencies (UNDP, FAO, UNIDO and ILO) led by the UNDP through UN SDG Acceleration fund. The experiences from SLSD and other regional companies will constitute an important element in this. During this period, there will be fact-finding, mapping and design focus where the stakeholders are involved in identifying opportunities to co-develop and pilot solutions in the two target sectors.

The overall objective of this project is to raise the awareness among private sector actors about SDGs and, in particular, ways business can benefit and contribute from their implementation in Albania. The project will seek to achieve this relying on the Swedish experience and investment focus and will facilitate business to business cooperation while at the same time supporting the private sector in delivery and monitoring of social and environmental impact. Making known good practices from Sweden will lead to better understanding and engagement on the SDGs and help identify opportunities to co-design and pilot solutions in the two selected sectors, agro-processing and textile.

The first output on increasing awareness on positive SDG practices has been achieved through the drafting of a Stocktaking papers on SDG practices and a Zero Roadmap reports on both sectors. The Stocktaking papers highlighted positive SDG practices and principles in the respective sectors. The Zero roadmap reports mapped out major sources of increasing sustainability in the value chain and areas with high potential to improve working conditions, productivity and efficiency of resource use, and mitigation of gender inequality. The ILO sustained Competitive and Responsible Enterprises (SCORE) programme piloted, which made baseline assessments of 19 TCLF enterprises and trainings of 15 of these. Six companies were selected to undergo the full RECP assessment introduced by UNIDO and to become the first RECP demonstration companies in the TCLF sector of Albania considering the representative sample for the size of enterprise sourcing of raw materials documentation of the sustainability activities in the TCLF sector affiliation to the employers associations application of finishing processes such as washing, bleaching, and dyeing. Experts and business representatives went on study tours from Albania to Sweden (12 participants from Albania, visits to 6 Swedish companies and Borås University, March 2023) and Tunisia (8 participants from Albania, visits to 5 Tunisian companies led by Tunisian expert institution, (May 2023). In the agroprocessing sector, 30 companies representing 6 different agroprocessing sectors (meat, dairy, fruits & vegetables, flour & bread, olive oil, and bottled water) were approached and consulted through focus group discussions (FGDs) and structured interviews.
The second output on increasing businesses awareness of the benefits of adopting SDG practices has been achieved through several activities. Among the results: - An ILO implemented training program aimed at improving working conditions and processes in Albania in line with SDG goals 5, 8, 9 and 12. - The business #2030 conference with over 250 participants was organised by UNDP which aimed to introduce innovative sustainable practices to Albanian businesses and highlight Swedish links. 9 Swedish speakers and 12 Swedish businesses participated. - 63 applications were received for SDG Business Pioneers Award and 15 companies were awarded. - For the agroprocessing sector, three focus group discussions and four roundtables were organized with representatives from the Albanian government, business, and academia. A total of 50 companies participated. For the textile and footwear sector, three round tables were organised.
